label: Choice-cell determination laws, from the definitions (inference)
rule: Unfold Cstit on the cell relation; a single cell is the whole scope; a selecting cell omits a rival history
meaning: Law 1 is the definition of Cstit read as cell-range exclusion. Law 2 is set algebra, using that the cell range lies in the realized range. Law 3: with one cell, Cstit of 'not y' quantifies over every history. Law 4: with one cell, selection says every history has the actual outcome. Law 5 uses excluded middle on the outcome of a cell member. Law 6: a history with another outcome lies outside the selecting cell, so the cell proposition is not necessary, and a single-cell level's cell contains that history. Law 7 transports Cstit along equal cells. Not a transcription: the definitions do not contain the laws.
